game.title: Rage (2011)
game.blurb: Post-apocalyptic first-person shooter with vehicle combat, from id Software (RAWG also lists Aspyr Media and Escalation Studios), published by Bethesda Softworks, released 2011-10-03. RAWG average playtime: 5 hours. Genres: Action, Shooter. Chapters follow the campaign locations named in the Steam achievements, plus chapters drawn from achievement themes.

chapters.title: Campaign: Ghost Hideout to Shrouded Bunker
chapters.summary: The first six campaign locations in the achievement list: Ghost Hideout, Wasted Garage, Mutant Bash TV, Dead City, The Well and Shrouded Bunker, plus a big night on Bash TV.

chapters.title: Campaign: Dead City Reverse to Blue Line Station
chapters.summary: The next six: Dead City Reverse, Authority Prison, Gearhead Vault, Power Plant, Jackal Canyon and Blue Line Station, then finishing the campaign. Spoiler-guarded.

chapters.title: The Scorchers Job Path
chapters.summary: Wellspring Tunnels, Hagar Caves, Refinery, Bash Canyon and Scorcher Base.

chapters.title: Difficulty Runs
chapters.summary: Finishing the campaign on Normal, Hard, Nightmare and Ultra Nightmare.

chapters.title: Races and Vehicles
chapters.summary: Campaign races and the Rage Cup, vehicle jumps, ATV field goals, destroying enemy cars and running over mutants.

chapters.title: Minigames
chapters.summary: Teague's decks, Tombstones, 5 Finger Filet, Strum, Roly-Poly, Video Poker and winning every minigame.

chapters.title: Collectibles, Jobs and 100%
chapters.summary: Playing Cards, Recipes and Schematics, Job Board quests, the Developer Graffiti Room and 100% completion.

chapters.title: Engineering and Combat
chapters.summary: Engineering items, Sentry Bots and Turrets, RC Bomb Cars, Wingsticks, the crossbow, mind control, the Railgun and Rebar ammo.

chapters.title: Legends of the Wasteland and Road RAGE
chapters.summary: The Legends of the Wasteland co-op missions and public Road RAGE matches.

StrategyWiki: no usable walkthrough, nothing used — https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Rage

notes: Backlog game, all-AAA pass: picked from RAWG's most-added list for its year across all genres (docs/PLAN.md section 2, genre filter widened 2026-10-23). RAWG's first search result is the expected 2011 entry "rage" (id 5636, released 2011-10-03), not Rage 2. The Steam store list has app 9200 ("RAGE"); its schema is named "ValveTestApp9200" (a placeholder name) and has 60 achievements, none hidden. StrategyWiki has "Rage" at completion stage 0 (marked as a perfect stub article); Gameplay, Walkthrough and Table of Contents are linked but no subpage is written, so it was not used. rage.fandom.com answers the API, redirecting to "RAGE", with about 44 linked articles; names only were looked at, nothing copied. The twelve campaign-location achievements are split into two halves of six in Steam list order (ach_25 to ach_36); unlock rates mostly fall in that order (82.8% for Ghost Hideout to 31.4% for Jackal Canyon), though Blue Line Station (36.1%) is higher than the three before it, so the exact order is not certain. The Scorchers job path achievements (ach_52 to ach_55 and ach_60) are a separate set; RAWG lists no additions for this game, so the chapter is named after the job path the descriptions name. "Bringin' Home the Bacon" (750 Dollars in one Bash TV episode) sits with Mutant Bash TV as a guess.
